subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or should default steering remain boundary-based?
rationale: The choice affects shared runtime semantics, message delivery expectations, session-state safety, backend compatibility, and possible new queue/config surface.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with explicit fallback and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steering as the supported default and limit current work to fixing messages reaching that existing boundary-based policy.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to stronger interruption semantics only after maintainer-approved compatibility and channel/runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with explicit fallback and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from the recent maintainer-labeled replacement path and adjacent session-state merge history.
